race: Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, where Bahrain comes to Malaysia and the title fight is already sweating in the roasting heat.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I love it because the news is hot, the upgrade is real, and nobody wants to be the one stuck in this Malaysian furnace.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So what is the story before we touch a single lap, and why does this Bahrain weekend in Malaysia feel so big?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Red Bull has brought an incredible upgrade to this roasting hot Malaysian event, and the whole mood is suddenly electric.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lewis himself says Max could be very tough to beat, which tells you exactly how much pressure is sitting on every car.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The headlines are already saying Verstappen takes his first pole position of twenty twenty six ahead of Hamilton, and that is a mouthful.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Russell adds that his confidence is back and growing, but he also says Red Bull looked strongest in practice, so trust is wobbling.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That brings us to the top three, and I am starting with Kimi Antonelli for Mercedes because the season says he is the one to beat.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He is championship leader, he has eight wins, and the Mercedes looks dominant enough to carry him even when the history gets awkward.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But wait, Kimi has just one race here, an average of eleventh, and zero podiums, so this is not his natural living room.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the quirk, but eight wins this season is a bigger story than one old weekend, and the Mercedes can still rewrite it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: My next top three pick is George Russell, and the circuit history helps him a lot because he has already been quick here.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Russell has a best of second here, an average of four point seven, and a podium already, so the track knows what he can do.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And his confidence is back, which makes that second place memory feel dangerous, especially if the heat plays to Mercedes.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Then there is Max Verstappen, and this is where I push back on you because the upgrade story is not just a headline.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Max has a win here, two podiums, an average of two point seven, and the Red Bull car can suddenly look like the one to beat.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lewis fears him, the pole position headline is his name, and Red Bull pace can turn a preview upside down before the first corner.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now the deep cut, because our tenth place pick is Carlos Sainz in the Williams, and that is the kind of gamble I like.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Low confidence, sure, but his historical form at this circuit is strong enough to keep him in the top ten when the heat bites.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a gamble, and I like it, because the midfield can suddenly bite in the heat and the big teams can have a wobble.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And if Mercedes and Ferrari both have a bad day, Carlos could be the one everyone remembers when the dust settles.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The rest of the top ten is all about momentum, with Hamilton, Leclerc, Norris, Piastri, Lawson, and Lindblad all in play.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: We also trust the Mercedes pairing to stay in front, but we know Red Bull and Ferrari can make this weekend ugly and brilliant.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The deep cut stays with Carlos, because a strong circuit memory can beat a low confidence label when the race gets spicy.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is our full top ten, all in one breath, Kimi Antonelli first, George Russell second, Max Verstappen third, Lewis Hamilton fourth, Charles Leclerc fifth, Lando Norris sixth, Oscar Piastri seventh, Liam Lawson eighth, Arvid Lindblad ninth, and Carlos Sainz tenth.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the heat, that is the pressure, and that is the upgrade battle we are watching from the pit wall in Malaysia.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Bahrain in Malaysia, the title on the line, and the race weekend is already electric. See you there.
